pilot_units.claim: The Hypershell design and current storefront organize product information near the purchase choices.
pilot_units.problem: A high-ticket device needs explanation alongside a purchase path.
pilot_units.why_it_matters: Customers can inspect the product and purchasing choices in one page context.

pilot_units.claim: A specific SilkGear section can be edited through the current Theme Editor.
pilot_units.problem: Merchant-maintained product education would benefit from configurable sections.
pilot_units.why_it_matters: Would show how the merchant can update content without code changes.

pilot_units.claim: The M7 PDP is composed from independently configurable OS 2.0 sections.
pilot_units.problem: A high-ticket eBike needs modular explanations for performance, fit and ownership.
pilot_units.implementation: The inspected M7 JSON template composes purchase, story, performance, specification, FAQ and related-product sections.
pilot_units.why_it_matters: The theme can present model-specific information without a single hard-coded PDP body.

pilot_units.claim: The current published M7 Theme Editor exposes a Specs Parameters section with three category blocks and configurable Geometry fields.
pilot_units.problem: Merchant updates to technical content need a verified workflow.
pilot_units.implementation: The inspected product-specs-parameters.liquid schema declares category fields, and its Liquid renders block settings into tab labels, spec rows and images. Save/reorder behavior was not tested.
pilot_units.why_it_matters: Connects the section schema to merchant-facing content controls for M7 technical information.
